reasoning: The core problem—quantifying how reproducible an LLM judge's verdicts are under resampling (seed, temperature, order) using psychometric test-retest reliability/ICC plus per-item flip rates, and relating low reliability to item categories—is already extensively addressed. "Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge" and "Can You Trust LLM Judgments? Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge" directly study judge self-inconsistency across repeated runs; the "Judge Reliability Harness" explicitly measures "stochastic stability under repeated sampling" and "1-Flip Consistency" (the proposed per-item flip rate), and "The Necessity of Setting Temperature in LLM-as-a-Judge" maps consistency vs. temperature/seed. The psychometric framing is not novel either: ICC(2,1) test-retest reliability is already applied to LLM evaluators, including per-attribute/per-item reliability stratification (some dimensions ICC 0.85-0.95, others 0.12-0.28) and item-response-theory diagnosis of which items drive low reliability (2602.00521). The only minor unexplored gap is the specific weak-judge scalable-oversight (debate/consultancy on QuALITY) setting and item-order perturbation, but weak-judge stability (Kenton et al.) and positional/order bias are themselves already studied.

evidence.title: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
evidence.summary: Directly studies self-inconsistency of LLM judges across multiple runs with identical prompts/hyperparameters, finding low self-reliability—the same resampling-instability problem the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Can You Trust LLM Judgments? Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Argues single-output LLM judging masks judgment variability and measures reliability across repeated runs; covers the central reproducibility-under-resampling question.

evidence.title: Judge Reliability Harness: Stress Testing the Reliability of LLM Judges
evidence.summary: Open-source harness measuring stochastic stability under repeated sampling and '1-Flip Consistency' (per-item flip rate), invariance to formatting/order, plus calibration—nearly the exact methodology proposed.

evidence.title: The Necessity of Setting Temperature in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Systematically maps verdict consistency and error rate against decoding temperature and seed, showing low temp gives near-perfect consistency—covers the temperature/seed variation axis of the proposal.

evidence.title: Diagnosing the Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge via Item Response Theory
evidence.summary: Applies psychometric item-level analysis to diagnose LLM judge reliability and identify which items drive low reliability—directly the 'which items drive low reliability' contribution.

evidence.title: How Model Size, Temperature, and Prompt Style Affect LLM-Human Assessment Score Alignment
evidence.summary: Uses ICC(2,1) two-way random-effects absolute-agreement test-retest reliability for LLM evaluators, establishing the exact psychometric ICC framing the proposal claims to borrow.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
evidence.summary: Establishes the weak-judge debate/consultancy oversight setting (incl. QuALITY) and notes weak-judge reliability/positional-bias issues, showing the proposed application context is already explored.
